## Energy Balance Diagram
::: {style="text-align:center;"}
![](figures/energy_balance_diagram.svg){width=70%}
:::
$$\text{Accumulation of Energy} = \text{Energy In} - \text{Energy Out}$$

::: {.fragment}
$$\frac{dE_{sys}}{dt} = \dot{E}_{in} + \dot{Q} + \dot{W} - \dot{E}_{out}$$
:::

## Energy accumulation in a system
$$\frac{dE_{sys}}{dt} = \dot{E}_{in} + \dot{Q} + \dot{W} - \dot{E}_{out}$$

Energy can be accumulated in a system as internal energy, kinetic energy, or potential energy.

. . .

Therefore, the total energy of a system is:
$$E_{sys} = U + E_k + E_p$$

## Energy entering and leaving a system
Energy can enter or leave a system within a mass flow as internal energy, kinetic energy or potential energy.

. . .

Therefore:
$$\dot{E}_{in} = \dot{U}_{in} + \dot{E}_{k,in} + \dot{E}_{p,in}$$
$$\dot{E}_{out} = \dot{U}_{out} + \dot{E}_{k,out} + \dot{E}_{p,out}$$

## Shifting mass in/out of the system
Work is needed when:

::: {.incremental}
- mass enters or leaves a system
- a system expands or compresses
:::
. . .

Must account for this work in the energy balance

. . .

When mass enters a system, internal energy *and* work is added.

## Enthalpy
The extra work can by accounted for by using enthalpy instead of internal energy

. . .

Enthalpy is **defined** as:
$$H = U + PV$$

::: {.callout-note}
## Key Term
**Enthalpy** ($H$) — a convenient state function defined by $H=U+PV$.
:::

## The General Energy Balance Equation {.scrollable}
Combining all the terms gives:
$$\frac{d(m_{sys}H_{sys})}{dt} = \dot{m}_{in} H_{in} - \dot{m}_{out} H_{out} + \dot{Q} + \dot{W}$$

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em"}
- $m_{sys}$ is the mass of the system (kg)
- $H_{sys}$ is the enthalpy of the system (J/kg)
- $\dot{m}_{in}$, $\dot{m}_{out}$ are the mass flow rates in or out of the system (kg/s)
- $H_{in}$, $H_{out}$ are the enthalpy of the streams in or out of the system (J/kg)
- $\dot{Q}$ is the rate of heat transfer to the system (W)
- $\dot{W}$ is the rate of work done on the system (W)
:::

## Multiple streams {.scrollable}
For multiple stream, include each term:

::: {style="text-align:center;"}
![](figures/energy_balance_diagram_multiplestreams.svg){width=60%}
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em"}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{d(m_{sys}H_{sys})}{dt} =& \dot{m}_{in,1} H_{in,1} + \dot{m}_{in,2} H_{in,2} + \dot{m}_{in,3} H_{in,3} \\
           & - \dot{m}_{out,1} H_{out,1} - \dot{m}_{out,2} H_{out,2}\\
           & + \dot{Q}_1 + \dot{Q}_2 - \dot{Q}_3\\
           & + \dot{W}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

## What affects Enthalpy ?
To solve the energy balance, must calculate the enthalpy of the flow streams and system.

. . .

Enthalpy is affected by:

::: {.incremental}
- Temperature changes
- Pressure changes
- Phase changes
- Formation and separation of solutions
- Reactions
:::

## Enthalpy changes

It is not possible to calculate absolute enthalpy values

. . .

Enthalpy changes can be calculated

. . .

Enthalpy can be calculated relative to a reference state

## Reference states

steady state single flow
